A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciNO research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original causal-discovery experiments on synthetic, Physics, Sachs, and BNLearn data, along with architectural comparisons and LLM-control experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports additional architectural ablations, causal-discovery baselines, runtime measurements, and LLM-control comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed SciNO architecture, multiplicative Learnable Time Encoding, probing strategy, and rank/CI control procedures remain unchanged. The added architectural variants are experimental comparisons, and Appendix A.3.3 documents the existing time-conditioned FNO architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ER graphs, Physics, Sachs, and four BNLearn graphs, including linear/nonlinear settings and masked-variable description scenarios. Physics and Sachs LLM results move from Table 4 to Table A.7; relabeling data as semi-synthetic does not change coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with CAM, SCORE, PC, GES, DAG-GNN, and GraN-DAG in Tables A.4–A.6. It also adds DiffAN with LTE and compares LLM control using SCORE or DiffAN evidence against SciNO evidence, substantially broadening comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new PC/GES comparison converts predicted graphs to CPDAGs and evaluates SHD-C. GPT-4o reporting drops v1's best-of-three selection in favor of ten-run summaries. Figure A.5 introduces runtime measurement with SciNO explicitly timed per epoch; the existing dataset construction and principal metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5.1 extends PE-versus-LTE analysis beyond ER graphs and adds additive-versus-multiplicative LTE and DiffAN-with-LTE ablations. V2 also tests how LLM-control performance depends on the evidence estimator and adds runtime scaling analysis. The earlier masked-description sensitivity study is retained as Table A.8.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 revise reported real/semi-synthetic repetitions from five to ten. The principal LLM comparison gains ten-run summaries and uncertainty terms, replacing single reported scores and GPT-4o best-of-three selection. SCORE-based control additionally specifies 1,000 bootstrap replicates. The ten-graph ER design was already stated in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline, ablation, control, and timing results and replaces many values in Tables 2–4. For example, Table 3's MAGIC-IRRI OD ranking reverses: CaPS/SciNO changes from 42/41.2 to 41/41.6. These are revised reported results, with changed repetition counts, rather than evidence of an improved method between versions. Existing ER results and the masked-description table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2's pointwise derivative-bound statement of Theorem 3.1 already appears as Theorem A.2 in v1. The accompanying material incorporates v1's Remark A.4 and expands explanation; the appendix assumptions, proofs, and Hessian derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The two central contributions and the abstract's 42.7% and 31.5% improvement claims remain. The introduction narrows the claimed maximum LLM-control OD reduction from 85% to 79%, reflecting the revised results.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablations as showing that LTE alone is insufficient and attributes LLM-control gains to both the control procedure and evidence quality. Section 4.1 qualifies improvement from all metrics to most metrics. The stated ANM and continuous-variable limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3.3 adds a layer-by-layer specification of time-conditioned FNO. Appendix A.4.3 adds a repository link and states that data, checkpoints, and training configurations are publicly available. Existing SciNO dimensions, layer counts, and GPU information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Four added references support GES, PC, GraN-DAG, and DAG-GNN, accompanied by discussion positioning SciNO against these methods. The introduction also adds a compatibility criticism of existing LLM approaches. The established related-work sections and central research positioning are largely retained.

P1.justification: Targeted revisions clarify the objective, theoretical motivation, and connection to LLM control. V2 adopts real/semi-synthetic terminology and inserts an additional-experiments section, shifting the LLM appendix from A.5 to A.6. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables A.1–A.7 and a runtime figure, substantially expanding the visual presentation of evidence. Table 4 is restricted to BNLearn, with the complete LLM comparison presented in Table A.7. Existing figures are relocated, table captions move above tables, and the original description-sensitivity table becomes Table A.8.

improvement.justification: The broader baseline comparisons and component/evidence-source ablations substantially address v1's limited validation of why SciNO helps. Repeated LLM summaries replace best-of-three GPT-4o reporting, and added access information strengthens reproducibility. Table A.3 inconsistently retains older SciNO values despite updates in Table 2, and per-epoch timings do not establish end-to-end speedups; these limitations temper but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
